The Federal Reserve Board on Thursday announced pricing, effective January 1, 2027, for payment services the Federal Reserve Banks provide to banks and credit unions, such as the clearing of checks, automated clearing house (ACH) transactions, instant payments, and wholesale payment and settlement services.

By law, the Federal Reserve must establish fees to recover the costs, including imputed costs, of providing payment services over the long run. The Federal Reserve expects to recover 101.5 percent of actual and imputed expenses in 2027, including the return on equity that would have been earned if a private-sector firm provided the services. Overall, price changes for 2027 will result in an estimated 1.4 percent average price increase for established, mature services.

In addition, the Federal Reserve Banks announced changes to streamline and adjust their check services. As described in the request for information on check services issued last year, the volume of checks processed by the Federal Reserve Banks is declining, but checks remain an important payment instrument for many consumers and businesses. The changes were informed by public feedback and ensure that the Federal Reserve Banks continue to provide check services efficiently. The adjustments include optimizing check processing windows during low-volume periods, increasing fees that banks and credit unions pay to process checks, and other operational updates. These changes do not impact consumers' and businesses' ability to pay with or receive checks and only impact how banks and credit unions process checks with Federal Reserve Banks.

The entire 2027 fee schedule for all of the Federal Reserve's payment services is published on FRBservices.org®. Additional information on the Federal Reserve's payments services, including service usage statistics, is available on the Board's website.

#2913. Tokenization platform Securitize gains 10% postmarket on Q3 results, move into asset-backed finance

Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

Miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

Securitize reinforced "certain areas of the company like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo said. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters."

Securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The company posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

Also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and announced the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo said.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

"We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth."

#2911. Falcons snap counts from another dreary Sunday against the Chiefs

It's snap counts time, whether you like it or not.

Beaux Collins getting 25 snaps was not something I expected, but then, the Falcons were down by a lot late. Collins got open enough twice in the end zone for Penix to look his way, but didn't come down with either target; the Falcons clearly like what he brings to the table enough to get him more involved at the likely expense of Zaccheaus and Blair going forward. This team is still searching for a reliable third receiver and Zachariah Branch is on injured reserve, so I'd still stump for seeing more of the reserve tight ends.

Otherwise, nothing here is really a surprise. These are familiar faces who just need to play better.

I thought we'd see more Brown and perhaps Bowman at safety, but Hellams did indeed step into Jessie Bates' spot and play nearly every snap. What's more, he was good, leading the team in tackles with no misses and acquitting himself in coverage on a day where most of the secondary got torched. I've long been a Hellams fan but thought he had essentially fallen out of this team's plans on defense; Hellams can play his way into a more significant role in 2027 if he keeps this up.

Pearce is still getting up to speed, and the team's edge rushers are providing sporadic pressure at this point; I fully recognize the job is tougher against Mahomes in the first place. Getting Pearce ramped up and Abdullah back in the rotation should help with that somewhat, but when Snowden is your most productive guy off the edge, you might be in a little bit of trouble. Zero offense intended!

Hughes has been effectively parked after struggling throughout the season, but this is now back-to-back weeks where Terrell and Henderson have been in hell, Terrell in particular. It's not completely out of the question for Hughes to find his way back into playing time if that continues, but the grimness of possibly benching one of your starters for a starter who was previously benched is not doing wonders for my mood right now.

A pretty successful day on special teams as the rest of the team fell apart, with Abdullah getting a massive workload. Moody delivered an onside kick and made all his tries, Bailey had a fine day punting, the coverage teams didn't allow any significant returns, and Blair had the play of the day grabbing the onside kick. The last couple of weeks have given me hope that this group is settling in, and the kicker change gives me more hope. I just hope "special teams were good" isn't the nicest thing I can say about this team the rest of the way.

The only other note is that the Falcons keep talking about numbers as a reason for parking player like Bowman and Avieon Terrell, the latter of whom was inactive this week; I'm not sure getting a handful of snaps out of TJ Quinn on special teams is worth sitting an effective defender.

#2910. Embiid, Brown have big scoring nights as Sixers down Nets, sweep back-to-back

BROOKLYN — That second half is probably best forgotten, but that's another win stacked. The Sixers escaped with a 135-123 win over the Brooklyn Nets Monday night.

Joel Embiid put up a season-high 37 points shooting 13-of-22 from the floor along with five rebounds. Tyrese Maxey had a more reserved night, going for 22 on 7-of-12 shooting with nine assists.

Jaylen Brown hit some big shots again as he finished with 31 points for the second straight night, going 9-of-19 from the field and pulling down 13 rebounds as well. VJ Edgecombe once again hit a big three late, finishing with 14 points along with nine rebounds and four assists shooting 4-of-10 from the floor. Julius Randle led the Nets with 33.

LeBron James missed the second half of the back-to-back with lower back management, as well as Adem Bona and Dom Barlow.

The Sixers wasted no time trying to create fast breaks as Maxey picked off an errant pass on the first possession of the game for an easy dunk. Edgecombe ran quickly off the Nets' first miss of the night, missing his layup but Dean Wade was there to put it back. Embiid had a weird start, picking up his first basket of the game picking some cherries down the end of the court. He and Edgecombe picked up a silly backcourt violation as Embiid did not get down the court all the way, but Edgecome still threw it to him.

With that being said, Embiid made four of his first seven shots, all of them being pretty easy looks near the basket. He finally knocked down a three later in the quarter. In some very intriguing rotation news, Jabari Walker played some four next to Embiid, despite being the most reliable backup five option at the moment. Expectedly, Walker did slide down to the five when Embiid first subbed out of the game.

The Nets' shot diet was similar to start the game, scoring 10 of their first 15 points from the paint, and putting some size next to Embiid in Walker didn't help that effort all that much. Walker picked up a hustle bucket on the other end, but couldn't finish the quarter after picking up two fouls. Wade replaced him to finish the quarter at center.

After a quiet start to the game, Brown took over the offense with Maxey and Embiid on the bench, getting to the line a couple of times. Edgecombe also had a strong take to the basket as the quarter closed, helping the Sixers get out to a seven-point cushion.

Anfernee Simons continued his stretch of tough shotmaking with a contested midrange pull-up to start the second. The Sixers got down the floor quick on their next trip, and Brown was able to find Simons wide open in the corner for a three. Brown got Danny Wolf to foul him on a three-point attempt, then stopped Wolf on a post-up, helping Philadelphia build an extended lead for the first time of the night.

It was a bit of a relief to see the Sixers just look flat out better than their opponent, and, yes, it took one of the worst in the league to do so. Edgecombe hit Walker with a high-low pass, and that gave him easy driving access on the next possession. Brown hit a nice crossover to leave his defender in his tracks and get to the basket. Embiid once again tried the self lob off the backboard, and thankfully enough players got in the paint to prevent him from attempting a dunk.

Embiid settled into a mode of just trying to draw a foul every time down the floor, which he was able to do pretty easily. Brooklyn is tall at a lot of positions but center, ironically, isn't one of them. Embiid took 10 free throw attempts as he put 24 points in the first half.

If there was one complaint for the half, it was that Nick Nurse only played eight guys against this Nets team on the second leg of a back-to-back. They set themselves up well for the end of bench guys to get plenty of run late, but it would have been nice to see some Labaron Philon Jr. minutes. Brown came off a screen to drill a three off a side out of bounds as the half came to a close. But Nolan Traore was able to draw a foul just before time expired, cutting the Sixers' lead to 19.

Embiid picked up right where he left off, opening the second half with a turnaround fadeaway. Wade kept doing all the little things, fighting for an offensive rebound to keep a possession alive for a Brown three. Maxey hit a quick stepback three and found Brown for another corner threee. It was a great start to the half offensively that offset Brooklyn coming away with three points on their first four possessions of the third.

That streak did end for the Nets, but they were able to build the tiniest bit of momentum after Embiid got called for a transition take foul on Randle. The Sixers sandwiched that with a couple of turnovers. The bucket they came up with to stop it was Embiid's best look of the night, driving past his defender and spinning to the hoop for an easy layup.

On the very next possession, Embiid went up aggressively but got blocked by Michael Porter Jr. and hit the deck hard flat on his back. He remained on the ground for a bit, long enough for the Nets to get an open three and have Nick Nurse call a timeout. As bad as it looked, Embiid seemed more concerned arguing with the officials that he should have been fouled during the timeout, and did remain in the game.

Maxey hit a three coming out of that timeout, but the Sixers had started to cool down as Brooklyn continued to inch back in it. They came within six before Brown buried a much needed midrange pull-up. After a rare stop he was able to get to the line on the next possession, but split the pair.

To make matters even trickier, Walker picked up his fourth foul which looked pretty cheap, but the Sixers had already lost their challenge earlier in the quarter. Moe Wagner might have missed both free throws, but Kentavious Caldwell-Pope missed a three on the ensuing possession and Porter drilled one coming back down the floor. Walker made a great finish once again getting found by Edgecombe and also got to the line and split a pair. He pumpfaked a defender that left him all alone on the wing and he buried a three as time expired to keep the Sixers up by 10 after three.

After the quarter started with a Wolf three to bring it back down to single digits, Brown picked up a foul on each end to bring him to four on the night as well. Edgecombe had a really nice driving dunk, but the Nets kept getting closer as the Sixers couldn't stop Randle.

As Brown was turning around with the ball, he didn't see Randle right behind him and slammed into him pretty hard. A foul was called but Brown hit the deck pretty quickly and was down for quite a bit. He left the game for three minutes of gametime but was able to return.

Walker tried to slide over and take a charge, but got whistled for his fifth, bringing Embiid back perhaps a minute or two earlier than intended. The Sixers got very lucky on the ensuing free throws. After Wolf missed both he got his own offensive rebound and missed the putback layup right at the rim. Embiid knocked down a pair of midranges, but got called for his fourth foul trying to block the shot of Day'Ron Sharpe.

Sharpe ended up missing both of those free throws as well, and Embiid followed that up with another pretty driving layup. Brown seemed to be OK as he knocked down a midrange, but the Sixers just couldn't keep the Nets down. Randle got an and-1 and Traore got to the line to remain within striking distance.

After some good ball movement, Maxey found Edgecombe wide open on the perimeter for a big three, but Traore came right down the floor and hit a three of his own. Despite some second chances the Sixers came up empty on the following poessession and Egor Demin came flying right down an open lane for a dunk, prompting a timeout from Nurse with the Sixers up only seven.

Demin hit a three after another empty Sixers possession to cut it to four. Embiid got the ball in the corner and calmly pumpfaked his defender, took a dribble and buried a much needed three in response. Embiid made more threes in this game (two) than he had over the past three weeks. Wade made a great play to block Randle and after Edgecombe won a jump ball and got fouled, the Sixers were able to win this one from the free throw line.

#2909. Anthropic IPO: For hundreds of billions of dollars flowing into AI startups, a big debut is a must

Artificial intelligence has propelled big gains in venture capital funds this year, and a flood of money — over $350 billion — into AI startups. Venture funds were up close to 18% through the first half of 2026, with 86% of U.S.-based VC investor money going into AI companies. With Anthropic set to make its public market debut this week at a reported valuation of $1.4 trillion, the market's reception to the deal and early trading in its shares may set the tone for the next leg in the private market AI boom.

It has been a period of increased volatility for tech stocks and the public market AI trade. In addition to concerns about balance sheet strength and valuation, midterm elections showed widespread public opposition to data centers, and the CEO scandal rocking Nvidia, the "central bank" of AI financing, has compounded risks in the sector.

But on the private side of tech investing, firms are closely watching how investors react to Anthropic's IPO. "I think that will end up guiding further intentions for the VC space," said Mike McLelland, managing director of investments within private markets at Cleveland, Ohio-based Clearstead. "Once you have a couple of good exits, it gives people a little more confidence in the realization story."

Read more: Everything you need to know about the Anthropic IPO

Anthropic is getting some deep-pocketed support for the deal. Altimeter Capital is aiming to invest $5 billion, according to its founder and CEO Brad Gerstner, who noted that was five times as much as he has ever invested in an IPO. "I think this is a cornerstone compounder for a long time," Gerstner told CNBC's "Halftime Report" on Monday. "It's where the trade is going."

Chip giants Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom, Nvidia, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company and Micron are all investing, as are Google and Microsoft.

The direction of the IPO market is important given that companies have been staying private longer than they did in the past and strategic exits have been relatively muted, McLelland said. A notable exception is Google's $32 billion acquisition of cloud security firm Wiz. That 2025 deal was Google's largest ever, overtaking its $12.5 billion purchase of Motorola in 2012.

VC gains have been concentrated in a small number of large funds that hold the biggest AI-linked companies. MSCI reports that the 10 largest holdings make up 22% of the value of its venture index.

That concentration comes amid improved performance.

Venture capital funds returned 17.8% in the first six months of 2026, according to Opto Investments, using proprietary and MSCI Private Capital Solutions data. Venture fund portfolio data is reported by fund general partners on a delayed basis. The six-month gains would equate to a full year return as high as 38% if the pace is maintained. It comes on the heels of a recent period of underperformance for the asset class, with a 6.19% return over five years, according to Juan Mier, lead analyst of fund strategies at PitchBook. Venture's 10-year average return is 13% annually, according to PitchBook. For the year ended March 2026, venture capital delivered a nearly 22% return, driven in large part by AI valuations, Mier said.

It is not just the largest AI companies that are venture-backed and tied to the IPO performance of the giants. Thousands of smaller companies that supply AI giants with infrastructure, component manufacturing, and data services, for example, have also seen their valuations rise quickly, said Jake Miller, co-founder of New York-based Opto Investments, which helps investment advisors design private investment programs.

Notably, AI captured $355.9 billion, or 86% of U.S. venture dollars in the first half of 2026, according to Clearstead analysis of PitchBook data. Globally, AI deal value reached $521.4 billion over the trailing twelve months. That's more than double the prior year, even as AI deal count fell 21.6% from the previous quarter.

Mier said venture capital returns are expected to moderate in the third quarter as valuations in the AI space in public markets have adjusted, and that flows to private markets eventually. "That may moderate returns for the second half of the year," he said. Anthropic's deal, reported to be on target for a $1.4 trillion valuation, is well below the $2 trillion deal value originally floated by bankers.

But amid the AI proliferation, industry participants expect VC to continue piquing investors' interest in the coming years. "It's been a great place to be, and it's going to be a great place to be given the momentum of venture companies," said Jeff Masom, head of U.S. distribution and global wealth management for private markets at Franklin Templeton, which manages several private markets investments.

That said, some investors are getting more discerning. "We see those opportunities among early-stage — Seed, Series A and Series B — companies rather than trying to get in on a later-stage company at a higher price," said Opto Investments' Miller. He's looking for opportunities to buy stakes in lower-valuation companies that could climb 10 times to 20 times from their current value through an IPO or acquisition.

Private infrastructure, meanwhile, returned 4.2% over the first six months of the year, a pace of about 8.5% a year, according to Opto Investments and MSCI data. "That is close to infrastructure's 10-year average of just under 10% a year," said Miller, but good enough to be the second-best among major private fund categories through the first half of 2026, ahead of private credit (2.6%) and buyout funds (1.4%). Private credit has been hit hard by fears about lending to software companies that could be rendered uncompetitive by AI, while private equity funds have struggled to sell portfolio companies at a profit this year, with a huge backlog of portfolio holdings.

But the AI boom has also benefited investors in infrastructure funds, given the needs for power, data centers, and fiber, areas where activity has been the strongest. "It's what's been driving most of those returns in the last 18 months or so," said Uday Karri, a member of MSCI's Private Capital Research team.

A recent MSCI report on private infrastructure showed that the index returned 11.9% over the 12 months through June 2026, compared with 7.7% for the median asset. Returns are based on MSCI's asset-level index, which measures underlying asset performance before fund fees, according to a spokesperson.

There's been tremendous growth in the past few quarters within infrastructure, and there continue to be opportunities for investors in the asset class, especially in AI-ready and liquid-cooled data centers, he said. Of course, midterm elections could slow new data center development through tighter permitting and regulation. In Texas, for example, Democratic governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned on a statewide moratorium on new data center permits. Shortly after her election, the new governor stressed in an interview with CNN that the key is creating state laws that protect Texas communities, not banning data centers.

With more political pressure related to data center construction, the infrastructure sector may benefit from expected opportunities outside the AI infrastructure build-out over the next several years. "Power, grid connections, water, cooling, fiber, and permitting are likely to shape where capacity can be delivered. Shifting trade routes, geopolitical disruption, and more frequent extreme weather are supporting investment in ports, railways, intermodal terminals, cold-storage networks, and other strategic transport infrastructure," according to a report from BlackRock's Preqin division.

Legislation is also advancing that could raise project costs for the biggest data centers, but potentially have more positive impacts on broader infrastructure projects. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA), a sweeping bill on energy infrastructure, is "the most comprehensive permitting bill to date," according to The Bipartisan Policy Center. If passed, it is expected to increase the speed of project permitting and reduce delays.

Here too, investors need to be discerning. "For investors, the key point is that asset selection can matter more than regional allocation. Larger portfolios can spread this dispersion across many assets and are more likely to track the index. Smaller portfolios hold fewer assets, so their results may differ materially from the index in either direction," MSCI wrote.

Private credit did perform better over the trailing 12 months ending in March, 8.3%, while real estate debt and core-plus strategies returned 7.2% and 5.1%, respectively, according to data from Preqin.

"The broader takeaway is that private markets are not moving in lockstep," Pei Yin, director at Preqin Private Markets Research, said in an email. "Venture capital has shown stronger return momentum, infrastructure continues to benefit from long-term investment themes, while private credit and selected real estate strategies have offered more income-oriented sources of return."

#2906. Roth 401(k) matches are 'surging,' report finds. What workers should know

Many more workers can now or will soon be able to accept a 401(k) match as a Roth contribution — giving them a new avenue to build a bucket of tax-free savings for retirement.

Historically, workers could only accept 401(k) match money from an employer as pretax, meaning they had to defer income taxes on those funds until they withdrew them in retirement.

Until a recent rule change, workers generally couldn't elect to receive a match as a Roth contribution. With Roth savings, investors don't get an up-front tax break — they pay income tax on the funds now but can take out the contributions and growth tax-free in retirement.

A law known as Secure 2.0, which former President Joe Biden signed into law in 2022, gave employers the option to add a Roth match as a feature of their 401(k) plans. If a plan offers a Roth match, it's not automatic; workers must opt in.

The number of employers that now let workers accept a 401(k) match or other employer contribution as Roth savings has "surged," according to a new report from the Plan Sponsor Council of America, a trade group representing employers.

About 42% of surveyed businesses that sponsored a 401(k) plan in 2025 have added or will add an option to accept employer contributions as Roth savings, according to an annual PSCA report published Nov. 10. That's more than double the share — about 20% — that did so in 2024, the report found.

Another 11% are still considering the option, according to the report.

The PSCA report is based on data from 753 employers that sponsor 401(k) plans of various sizes.

"My guess is we will continue to see [the share] increase," said Hattie Greenan, the group's research director. "Roth is becoming mainstream," she said.

But just because employees have the Roth match option available to them doesn't mean it will be their best option.

There are pros and cons to pretax and Roth savings, and the right choice can vary from person to person, financial advisors said.

"[Roth] is not a bad idea if you're not so worried about your taxes today," said Philip Chao, a certified financial planner and chief investment officer at Experiential Wealth, based in Cabin John, Maryland. "It's personal preference."

While there are ample benefits to saving at least some money as Roth funds in a 401(k), most investors opt against it.

In fact, while almost all 401(k) plans already allow workers to save part of their paychecks as a Roth contribution, only a quarter of workers actually do so, according to the PSCA report.

"The list of cons may be short for Roth 401(k)s, but missing tax deferral is a big one," according to a May article written by Fidelity, a retirement plan administrator. "When faced with a choice of paying more tax now or later, most people choose to pay later, hence the low participation rates for Roth 401(k)s."

Tax deferral has long been a "key driver" of retirement savings, Fidelity said.

Saving on a pretax basis effectively increases a worker's take-home pay. It also reduces their adjusted gross income today, and may therefore positively impact the calculation of eligibility for child tax credits, financial aid for college or federal aid, according to Fidelity.

A Fidelity example shows the financial benefit of an up-front tax break: Let's say a saver with a $75,000 annual income in the 22% federal income tax bracket makes a $400 monthly 401(k) contribution. Making the full contribution as Roth would reduce their paycheck by $400. Making the contribution into a traditional — i.e., pretax — 401(k) would reduce their paycheck by just $312.

For those who can stomach the up-front tax hit, Roth provides for powerful tax-planning opportunities in future years, according to financial advisors.

"Roth gives you a lot more flexibility at retirement," Chao said. "But you have to be OK with paying years of tax on it first. It's never something for nothing. There's always a trade-off."

For example, the government doesn't require investors to withdraw a minimum amount from Roth accounts in retirement, as it does with pretax savings. These annual "required minimum distributions," or RMDs, generally start at age 73 for traditional 401(k)s and IRAs, among other accounts.

Additionally, withdrawing money from Roth accounts in retirement can help limit taxes on Social Security benefits and reduce Medicare premiums, which are based on taxable income. Roth withdrawals don't count as taxable income.

Retirees can also make strategic withdrawals from Roth accounts in certain years to avoid jumping into a higher federal or state income tax bracket, advisors said.

"Once you pay the taxes [on a Roth contribution], the government is out of your hair," Chao said. "There's no amount you must draw out. It's your money; it's all tax-free when you take it out."

For example, many investors must wait until at least age 59 1/2 to withdraw funds tax-free from a Roth 401(k) account. Additionally, due to a so-called five-year rule, investors must have had Roth 401(k) funds for at least five years to make a tax-free withdrawal.

Because Roth employer matching contributions are included in the saver's income, investors should ensure they have enough tax withheld from their paycheck to cover the income tax, according to Fidelity.

The ultimate goal for savers choosing whether to make Roth or pretax contributions is to pay income taxes when their tax rate is lowest, advisors said.

For example, Roth savings can work well for younger savers over the long term if they anticipate their incomes — and tax rates — will grow over time, said Andrew Bachman, director of tax and retirement income on Fidelity's financial solutions team.

Similar logic applies to people who plan to move from a low-tax to a high-tax state in retirement, such as from Texas to California, he said.

While it's impossible to know future tax rates, investors can hedge by splitting contributions between both types of accounts, advisors said.

Similar to contributions, workers may be able to split a 401(k) match between pretax and Roth savings. However, workers will be constrained by what their employer does and doesn't allow, Chao said.

#2900. What's ahead for AI financing after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang departs

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure hasn't produced a broad shock to the credit market, but it is putting the company's role as a financier of artificial intelligence infrastructure under scrutiny.

Huang, who stepped down Thursday amid an espionage and adultery scandal, built Nvidia into an AI powerhouse in the 33 years since he co-founded the company. Chief financial officer Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as the company searches for a permanent chief executive.

Nvidia not only supplies its graphics processing units to hyperscalers and tech giants, it also provides financing to other companies to help the industry expand. That could all change.

"Although we expect the company to fulfill all of its previously announced commitments, we believe that going forward, it may be more difficult for the company to negotiate new multi-party investments among ecosystem partners at the same scale it has done up to this point," Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider said in a note Thursday.

The news of Huang's resignation comes after investors were already concerned about the massive amount of debt being taken on to fund AI infrastructure.

Tech bond yields have risen and spreads have widened on credit default swaps, most notably in lower-rated names. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier.

On Friday, the yield on Nvidia's 4.5% bond due in 2031 sat at 5.717%, nearly 5% higher week to date. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

Tech stocks slumped Friday with the Nasdaq 100 closing down 1.2% as markets continued to digest the Nvidia news. Yields on hyperscaler bonds ticked slightly higher on Friday, signaling the broader concern about AI debt lingers.

It's the smaller AI companies that could ultimately see an impact if Nvidia makes any changes to its AI financing. The company had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July.

Neoclouds CoreWeave, Nebius and IREN are all in Nvidia's portfolio. Their shares were down sharply Thursday.

CoreWeave, which has become the poster child for AI debt fears, saw its bond yields retreat after its quarterly earnings on Tuesday eased investor concerns. The yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 14.79% on Friday after climbing to 16.7% last week. The spread on its five-year CDS also dropped more than 17% week to date, although it remained above 1,000 — which is generally considered a sign of distress.

It remains unclear how Nvidia's support for those companies may change, said CreditSights analyst Andy Li.

"We don't know what the ultimate strategy for Nvidia is going to be coming out the other side," he said.

"However, I think directionally, just given the fact that Jensen was so crucial in selling the Nvidia story and being a very aggressive deal maker, it's likely that a lot of this creative deal-making and circular financing and equity and credit support is going to moderate," he added.

CoreWeave CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC Wednesday, before Huang's departure, that Nvidia "is not one person."

"There are thousands of people over there that interface with thousands of people at my company every day. They integrate on the technology. They integrate on the physical infrastructure. They integrate on the networking," he said in an interview with "Squawk on the Street." "They have been a great partner for us for years. They will continue to be a great partner for us."

Bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, doesn't see any big changes in terms of Nvidia's relevance or its ability to finance for now. As CFO, Kress was involved in the financing deals, and the search for a permanent CEO is going to take some time, he noted.

The real issue is just how much money the company will want to lend for AI financing, rather than, say using its hundreds of billions in free cash flow for other purposes, like share buybacks, capex, or acquisitions.

"Big companies like Nvidia and Meta, they're holding all the cards," he said. "When they decide that the game is over, that's it — it's going to be curtains for some of these smaller companies."

— CNBC'S Kif Leswing and Isabel O'Brien contributed reporting.

#2897. Ukraine damages Putin’s prized Crimea bridge as Zelenskyy lauds ‘unprecedented operation’

Ukraine has damaged the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, delivering a symbolic blow to President Vladimir Putin as Kyiv reels from strikes on its own infrastructure.

Sergey Aksyonov, the Russia-installed governor of Crimea, confirmed that the strategically important bridge, which had been briefly closed on Monday, was attacked overnight for the second time in two days.

Videos and photos circulating on social media appeared to show the partial destruction of the bridge, with one section having collapsed into the water. CNBC was unable to independently verify the footage.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the attack as an "unprecedented operation" several weeks in the making, with Ukraine's defense forces, security services and weapons manufacturers involved.

"Russia strikes our infrastructure every day, including bridges in Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro, Kyiv, and the Odesa region," Zelenskyy said Tuesday on X.

"We are restoring our infrastructure. But we are also reminding Russia that war will always return to where it began. Ukraine's defensive capabilities are strong and will remain so, and we will never leave terror against our cities and people unanswered," he added.

Train and vehicle traffic was suspended due to the attack. No injuries have been reported.

Ukraine has repeatedly targeted the bridge since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in early 2022.

A 12-mile crossing of road and railways, the Kerch Bridge is one of Putin's signature projects. The crossing, sometimes referred to as the Crimean bridge, was built on his orders shortly after the Kremlin forcibly annexed Crimea in 2014 to support Moscow's claims to the territory.

Rail traffic on the bridge was opened on one track, Russia's Ministry of Transport said in a statement via Telegram on Tuesday, while restoration work continues on the second section.

The co-owner and chief engineer of Ukrainian missile and drone maker Fire Point, Denys Shtilierman, appeared to confirm the company's role in the attack, following reports that a Ukrainian Flamingo cruise missile was used in the strike.

"We dedicate this to the memory of our friends and colleagues Andriy and Yuriy, without whom this would not have been possible. R.I.P.," Shtilierman said via X on Tuesday. A spokesperson at Fire Point separately confirmed the company's role in the attack.

Analysts at the Institute for the Study of War, a Washington-based think tank, said Ukraine's attacks on the Kerch Bridge were likely part of Kyiv's ongoing and systematic strike campaign aimed at denying Russian forces the use of major ground lines of communication via Crimea.

Russian forces, meanwhile, struck two bridges crossing the Dnipro River in Kyiv.

Vitaliy Klitschko, the mayor of Ukraine's capital, said via Telegram on Tuesday that specialists were working to assess the extent of the damage to the North and South bridges.

Klitschko said Russian attacks on Kyiv overnight had also caused disruptions to water and heating supplies.

The strikes come ahead of Putin's trip to China this week for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, where a trilateral meeting with U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping is planned on Thursday.

Asked whether Ukraine's latest attacks might be connected to the upcoming trilateral summit, Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said this could not be ruled out.

"Combat operations continue, and our military is striking targets that are somehow connected to Ukraine's military-industrial complex. And Ukraine is continuing its terrorist attacks," Peskov said, according to Russian state news outlet Ria Novosti.

#2895. Nets can’t finish comeback vs LeBron-less Sixers, lose 135-123

I went to watch my New York Giants host the Washington Commanders at MetLife this past Thursday. They gave up a game-winning score with less than a minute to go. Last night, as a proud Syracuse alum, I went to watch the Orange face St. John's at Madison Square Garden. They ended up losing by 17 after leading by three at half.

Desperately hoping to see a winning performance, I knew the Barclays Center was the place for me to go on Monday evening!

Yes, I'm being sarcastic … a bit cynical, too. As expected, the Nets lost tonight to the Philadelphia 76ers. However, they did battle, so if you haven't soured on morale victories yet, read on.

With Michael Porter Jr. returning from a one-game absence due to personal reasons, the Nets first five in game No. 13 featured MPJ alongside Nolan Traoré, Egor Dëmin, Julius Randle, and Day'Ron Sharpe. The Sixers began with Jaylen Brown, Tyrese Maxey, VJ Edgecombe, Joel Embiid, and Dean Wade. LeBron James sat this one out to rest his back on the back-end of a back-to-back.

Like Joseph Quinn and Chris Evans, Michael Porter Jr. and Julius Randle had the hot hand at different times tonight, but both did simultaneously in the early going. The pair of vets combined for 13 of Brooklyn's first 19 points to keep the Nets in it as Joel Embiid mismatched his way to 13 opening quarter points. They were also helped by Keon Ellis, who returned to the rotation after playing just seven minutes of garbage time vs Memphis on Saturday. Eager to stay out of the dump, he went 2-of-2 from deep in the period with two blocks and a steal.

But even as Ellis helped the Nets post 46/43 splits in the first, they still trailed 33-26 after it. At the other end, whatever the Sixers weren't getting on their first try, they were on their second or third. Philly outscored the Nets in second chance points during the opening frame 10-3. Jaylen Brown, still haunting us just in a new rival's uniform, pulled down three offensive boards to help out on that front. He also finished the game with 31 points, 13 total rebounds, five assists, a steal, and a block.

Nolan Traoré chose to take the blame for the weak defensive start postgame.

"Don't be passive in the first minutes of the game," he said. "I've got to be the one, the one pushing, the one putting pressure on them, and not the inverse. So yeah, that's it."

The Nets did improve on the offensive glass in the second, not because they boxed out better or went with a bigger lineup, but because their opportunities to defend their own glass vanished. The 76ers began the second shooting 9-of-11 from the field, eventually going 14-of-21 by the end of the period and 4-of-7 from deep.

Brooklyn, who shot a less impressive 12-of-26 from the field and 0-of-6 from deep, looked out of position both on defense and just as Philly's opponent in a competitive setting. Whenever the Sixers weren't swinging the ball around to stretch Brooklyn out and get favorable looks, they were hitting off isolation takes that just put a sweltering and oppressive spotlight on Brooklyn's lack of comparable talent.

In fairness, these are the "super" Sixers, even without King James. Remember when the Nets had a team like that? That was fun.

Anyway, Philly led 78-57 at the break. Randle led the team by a wide margin at that point, pitching in 18 points on 7-11 shooting. With eight points in the second, Traoré worked his way to 10 points and two assists on 3-6 shooting. However, the other young guards struggled in what was arguably their worst collective game so far. Mikel Brown Jr. and Egor Dëmin combined for zero points on 0-6 shooting and two turnovers at half. Brown only made one basket the whole game, going 1-7 from the field, but did drop five assists with only one turnover.

Dëmin's first points of the night didn't come until the 6:25 point of the game, and although tardy, their timing was appreciated. After Randle kept Brooklyn hanging around with another eight points in the opening half of the third, Porter Jr. and Day'Ron Sharpe teamed up for a block on Embiid that sprung a transition opportunity, leading to a Dëmin three that cut the deficit to 10.

And after that, Michael Porter Jr. picked up the baton. He got 12 of his 25 points for the game in the third to bring Brooklyn even closer. A large percentage of his makes came via the dribble-handoff sequences Brooklyn often runs for him, but the biggest was a straight up heat check, which made it a six point game with about a minute to go…

After those six blanks in the second, the Nets had gone 5-7 from three in the third. They also bounced back on the glass to win by a 13-6 margin in the period.

"I think we just played harder," Traoré said. "We grabbed more rebounds, even if it wasn't enough, but it was just like a team effort to get stops together and then run."

Traoré enjoyed another solid night, contributing with a career-high 23 points alongside eight assists, two steals and just two turnovers while shooting 7-12 from the field and 2-4 from deep. Randle agreed with his assessment that the Nets played harder in the second half.

"Just punch first," he said. "Like in the second half, we punched first, and set the tone. I think we have to start every game like that punch first approach."

Randle was right about that and just about everything tonight. He had his best game as a Net, finishing with 33 points, six rebounds, an assists, two steals, and a block while shooting 13-20 from the field and 2-4 from deep.

The Sixers went two for one down the stretch of the third, with the latter offensive possession generating a Jabari Walker three at the buzzer to put them back up 10 entering the fourth. But the Nets were far from discouraged. Danny Wolf got the scoring started there with a drive-and-kick three from Noah Clowney. Julius Randle added on in transition shortly after that got it down to five with 9:54 to go.

But down the stretch, Philly started spamming the Joel Embiid x Tyrese Maxey pick-and-roll, which was as calming for the Sixers as it was effective in producing points. Bit by bit, Philly inched further ahead to lead 122-111 with 2:56 remaining.

But while quiet for most of the game, Egor Dëmin did have something to say before Philly could ice things. After the Sixers had slowly but surely rebuilt a double digit lead, Dëmin quickly and impulsively brought it back to two after sneaking inside for a finish at the rim before trotting down on the next possession and sinking a pull-up triple with 1:14 to play.

It felt a bit like the Orlando game last year, only this time, the visiting team's All-Star hit the big three to essentially end it a few seconds earlier.

The next time down the floor, Embiid splashed a corner three, which pushed the lead back up to five with 52 seconds remaining. In a monster game, the Philly big man finished with 37 points, five rebounds, an assists, a steal, and two blocks while shooting 13-22 from the field. Dëmin finished tonight with nine points, four assists, and three rebounds while shooting 3-10 from the field and committing five turnovers. He and Brown Jr. were still a combined of 12 points on 4-of-17 in 44 minutes.

"I'm just trying to do the best for the team, whatever's in front of me," Dëmin said. "I don't know. I'm just trying to enjoy the game, go out there and hoop with my friends, and some days are like that, some are different, and hopefully I can get more of the good days then bad days, so kind of trying to approach it with this kind of attitutde."

To stave off the comeback, Philly only need to take care of business at the line. Edgecombe and Maxey handled all the paperwork, going 7-8 from the line as the clock ran out.

It wasn't just finisher move from Philly, but another lesson for the Nets in what they need to patch up. With Brooklyn's offensive renaissance in the second half, they ended up shooting better from deep for the game by nearly five percentage points. They shot worse from the field by just over one. However, they left 12 points at the line, shooting 22-34 for the game.

"I don't want to go to the players and go, 'yeah, make free throws,' and then you go there and you're like nervous," Fernández said. "You know, obviously, I don't want to shoot 64%. If we shoot better, we probably have a bigger chance, but I know our guys are good shooters, and they're going to make free throws. We're going to concentrate and make sure we believe that all of them are gonna go in."

Final: Philadelphia 76ers 135, Brooklyn Nets 123

Julius Randle collided with Jaylen Brown in the fourth quarter took a shot to the face. He stayed in the game, but didn't mince words about it postgame. Nevertheless, we highly doubt he'll miss any time.

"It feels terrible, to be honest," Randle said. "But I'm fine. It just went to track on me, he turned, and didn't see me. Just kind of collided, but it's fine."

Julius Randle tied his season high with 33 points. It was his second 30-point game this season.

Day'Ron Sharpe recorded five assists in his sixth straight game, extending the longest such streak in Nets history.

Nolan Traore tied his career high with 23 points. It was also his high for the season thus far.

The Nets play the Chicago Bulls Wednesday night at Barclays Center, starting at 7:30 p.m. EST. It will be Nic Claxton's first return to Brooklyn after the three team June trade that sent him and a second rounder (Isaiah Evans) to Chi-Town and Julius Randle and a first (Joshua Jefferson.)

#2893. Deutsche Bank shares sink as whistleblowers reveal Epstein payments, Trump tax leak, Russia bets

Deutsche Bank shares fell sharply in early trading on Tuesday after whistleblowers leaked about 15 million files from the German lender, with media reports revealing alleged historic failures across its risk management and financial crime controls.

These include suspicious payments linked to late financier and convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, and accidental leaks of President Donald Trump's tax statements.

The leaks contain board minutes, emails, internal investigations and other material that point to systemic failures across the Frankfurt-listed lender's business functions stretching back two decades.

Shares in Deutsche Bank were 4.7% lower by 9:20 a.m. E.T., having fallen more than 6% in early trade in Frankfurt.

Deutsche Bank processed $582 million in suspicious payments linked to Jeffrey Epstein, far more than previously known, the FT reported. Suspicious payments are not, by themselves, proof that every transaction was criminal.

The German lender also mistakenly leaked details of U.S. President Donald Trump's taxes in March 2017, during his first term in office, the FT said. The blunder — described by CEO Christian Sewing, who was then Deutsche's private banking head, as "an awful mistake" — was kept secret from the White House.

The wide-ranging investigation — which was led by a consortium of more than 200 journalists worldwide including the FT, Der Spiegel and Le Monde — also said Deutsche Bank had failed to offboard around 28,000 problematic investment bank clients who had been identified for removal by early 2018.

It also alleges that the bank concealed information around cost targets in 2021, when external monitors in New York reportedly warned that Deutsche's risk appetite was running ahead of controls.

The files also contain details of the bank's relationships with oligarchs and transactions that the investigation links to Russian money-laundering concerns. It was these ties that motivated whistleblowers to send the information to Indian journalist Josy Joseph and South African journalist Khadija Sharife.

The reports once again put Deutsche Bank's risk management practices and controls under the spotlight following years of regulatory scrutiny.

The bank — which has been raided multiple times by German officials this year — has, since 2012, paid out some 18.6 billion euros ($20.5 billion) in settlements over alleged market manipulation, money laundering, mis-selling and misrepresentation, among other things, the FT said.

In a statement, Deutsche Bank said the issues detailed in Tuesday's media reports go back many years.

"Where relevant, we reviewed these matters at the time and worked closely with regulators," the lender said.

The bank said it has undergone a "fundamental transformation" under CEO Christian Sewing, pointing to 7 billion euros of investment in its risk controls between 2019 and 2025.

"Deutsche Bank is a different bank today and remains focused on executing its strategy which has proven successful, as evidenced by record profits in 2025 as well as in recent quarters."

CNBC has reached out to BaFin, Germany's financial regulator, for comment.
